title: Earth Microbiome Project High Throughput DNA Extraction Protocol
author: Lisa Marotz1
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pdmdi46

steps.title: Pellet beads on PowerBead Plate
steps.instruction: Remove the PowerBead® DNA Plate (Bead Plate) from the QIAGEN® MagAttract® PowerSoil® DNA KF Kit (384) and centrifuge it for 1 minute at 2500 × g to pellet the garnet beads before adding any sample.

steps.title: Remove and set aside Square Well Mat
steps.instruction: Take the Square Well Mat off the Bead Plate, place it in a sterile location, and keep it aside; it will be replaced after the samples are added.

steps.title: Add sample material to wells
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate sample to each well of the Bead Plate: 0.1–0.25 g soil, 1 swab head, or ≤250 µl liquid per well.

steps.title: Add Bead Solution/RNase A
steps.instruction: Pipette 750 µl of Bead Solution/RNase A Solution into every well of the Bead Plate.

steps.title: Add SL Solution and seal plate
steps.instruction: Add 60 µl of SL Solution to each well, then place the Square Well Mat back onto the plate and press tightly to obtain a complete seal of every well; use gloved hands and a plate‑sealing roller if needed.

steps.title: Incubate sealed plate at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Put the sealed Bead Plate(s) in a 65 °C water bath for 10 minutes (do NOT submerge the plate). Prepare an ice container large enough to surround the plate for the later cooling step.

steps.title: Prepare plate for shaking
steps.instruction: Remove excess water from the plate, verify that all wells remain sealed, then sandwich each Bead Plate between two Adapter Plates (QIAGEN catalogue 11990) and fasten the assembly to a 96‑well plate shaker (e.g., QIAGEN TissueLyser® II, catalogue 85300). Balance the shaker if only one plate is used by adding an empty PowerBead® DNA Plate to the opposite station.

steps.title: Shake plate at 20 Hz
steps.instruction: Shake the assembled plates at 20 Hz for 20 minutes, ensuring the Adapter Plates are securely positioned and no parts rub against the shaker.

steps.title: Centrifuge and add IR Solution
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Bead Plate(s) at room temperature for 6 minutes at 3220 × g (or 4500 × g if required). While centrifuging (or during shaking), dispense 450 µl of IR Solution (Inhibitor Removal Technology® Solution) into each well of a clean 1 ml Collection Plate and cover with the provided clear Sealing Tape.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to IR collection plate
steps.instruction: Remove the lysate‑containing Bead Plate(s) from the centrifuge, discard the Square Well Mat, then remove the Sealing Tape from the IR‑Solution Collection Plate. Transfer ≤640 µl of lysate from each well of the Bead Plate into the corresponding well of the IR‑Collection Plate and mix gently by pipetting up and down four times (the lysate may contain particulate matter).

steps.title: Seal and incubate IR plate at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Apply a new piece of clear Sealing Tape to the IR‑Collection Plate (repeat for a second Bead Plate if present) and incubate the plate(s) at 4 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge IR plate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the IR‑Collection Plate(s) at 3220 × g for 6 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to new collection plate
steps.instruction: Remove the Sealing Tape, then transfer the entire supernatant (~850 µl) from each well to a fresh sterile 1 ml Collection Plate (Plate #2), avoiding the pellet. Discard the used IR‑Collection Plate(s). Some pellet material may be carried over.

steps.title: Seal and centrifuge second collection plate
steps.instruction: Seal Plate #2 with new Sealing Tape and centrifuge at 3220 × g for 6 minutes.

steps.title: Aliquot supernatant to KingFisher plates
steps.instruction: Remove the Sealing Tape from Plate #2, then transfer 450 µl of the supernatant to a clean KingFisher™ Deep Well 96 Plate (Plate A) and the remaining 400 µl to a second KingFisher™ Deep Well 96 Plate (Plate B). Discard Plate #2. If the workflow is to be stopped here, seal both KingFisher plates with foil (not kit Sealing Tape) and store at 4 °C overnight, but no longer than one day.

steps.title: Start KingFisher Flex purification program
steps.instruction: Launch the ‘KF_Flex_MoBio_PowerMag_Soil_DNA’ program on the KingFisher™ Flex robot, ensuring the protocol uses both lysate aliquots. If required, download the script from https://mobio.com/products/dna-isolation/soil/powermag-soil-dna-isolation-kit.html and transfer it to the instrument.

steps.title: Prepare magnetic bead suspension
steps.instruction: For each 96‑well plate to be processed, suspend 2 ml ClearMag® Zorb Reagent in 45 ml ClearMag® Binding Solution in a clean reservoir; pipette up and down thoroughly to disperse the beads. Mix the suspension immediately before adding to samples because the beads settle quickly.

steps.title: Prepare RNase A/PowerBead solution
steps.instruction: In a sterile reservoir, combine 400 µl RNase A Solution (25 mg ml⁻¹, catalogue 700511) with 75 ml PowerBead® Solution for each 96‑well plate. PowerBead® Solution contains guanidinium thiocyanate (CAS 593‑84‑0, <10 % w/w) and must be handled as hazardous waste.

steps.title: Check and warm SL Solution
steps.instruction: Inspect the SL Solution (lysis buffer). If a precipitate is visible, heat the solution at 60 °C until fully dissolved; the solution can be used while still warm.

steps.title: Decontaminate work surfaces and equipment
steps.instruction: Remove nuclease and nucleotide contamination from all work surfaces and instruments with RNase AWAY™ (Thermo Scientific catalogue 700511), then wipe with 70 %–100 % molecular‑biology‑grade ethanol and let dry. Turn on a water bath to 65 °C.

steps.title: Clean pipette and prepare tips
steps.instruction: Clean the multichannel pipette (capacity up to 1000 µl) and ensure the tips fit the round wells of the Collection Plate; the Knight Lab uses Rainin™ tips (catalogue RT‑1000F).

steps.title: Prepare wash and elution plates
steps.instruction: For each 96‑well plate, aliquot 500 µl ClearMag® Wash Solution into each well of three clean KingFisher™ Deep Well 96 Plates, and add 100 µl Solution EB (elution buffer) to each well of one KingFisher™ 96 KF Microtiter (200 µl) Plate. Note that 65 µl Solution EB is used for low‑biomass samples.

steps.title: Prepare binding solution reservoir
steps.instruction: For each 96‑well plate, add 47 ml ClearMag® Binding Solution to a separate clean reservoir.

steps.title: Add beads to lysate plates
steps.instruction: To one KingFisher™ Deep Well 96 Plate containing lysate, add 470 µl ClearMag® Zorb Reagent mixed with ClearMag® Binding Solution to each well. To the remaining lysate‑containing Deep Well plate(s), add 470 µl ClearMag® Binding Solution alone to each well.

steps.title: Load KingFisher Flex deck
steps.instruction: Follow the on‑screen prompts to load the deck in this order: tip comb, elution plate, the three ClearMag® Wash Solution plates, the lysate plate with ClearMag® Binding Solution (Bind 2), and the lysate plate with ClearMag® Binding Solution + Zorb Reagent (Bind 1).

steps.title: Run KingFisher program
steps.instruction: Start the selected KingFisher Flex program; it will run automatically for approximately 65 minutes with no user intervention.

steps.title: Collect and seal eluted gDNA
steps.instruction: When the program finishes, remove the gDNA‑containing elution plate and seal it with an appropriate storage seal (not the kit Sealing Tape).

steps.title: Dispose waste and finalize
steps.instruction: Follow the prompts to cycle through each station, discard all liquids as hazardous chemical waste, and discard the emptied plates. The purified gDNA is now ready for downstream applications.

steps.title: Optional stop and store plate
steps.instruction: If the workflow is paused after sample addition, reseal the loaded Bead Plate with the Square Well Mat, store the plate at –20 °C, and mark the orientation of the mat (e.g., write “A1” with a VWR® Lab Marker, catalogue 52877‑310).
